fault: The keycap on the G key is missing, leaving the bare switch and its cross-shaped stem exposed.
diagnosis: The G keycap has come off, so the switch underneath is bare. I'll have you power the board down, check the switch and socket are fine, and press a matching keycap back on.
safety_notes: Unplug the USB-C cable before touching the exposed switch.
Touch grounded metal first to discharge static before handling the board.
Do not force the keycap on if it does not line up with the stem.

steps.title: Unplug the keyboard
steps.instruction: Unplug the USB-C cable from the back of the keyboard. Touch grounded metal first.
steps.expected_visual_state: No cable is plugged into the USB-C port and the backlight is off.
common_mistakes: Leaving the cable plugged in while working on the key.
Reaching for the board without grounding yourself first.

steps.title: Check the bare G switch
steps.instruction: Look at the G position and check the switch is seated flat with its cross-shaped stem upright. Press the stem a few times.
steps.expected_visual_state: The bare G switch sits flush with neighbouring switches and its stem springs back after each press.
common_mistakes: Not noticing a cracked or tilted switch.
Pressing the stem sideways instead of straight down.

steps.title: Clear dust from the G switch
steps.instruction: Blow around the exposed G switch with compressed air. Keep the can upright.
steps.expected_visual_state: The G switch and the plate around it are free of dust and debris.
common_mistakes: Tilting the compressed air can so liquid sprays out.
Leaving debris around the stem that stops the keycap seating.

steps.title: Place the G keycap
steps.instruction: Line up the G keycap with the cross-shaped stem, with the legend facing you. Press it straight down until it is fully seated.
steps.expected_visual_state: The G keycap is on the G position at the same height and angle as the surrounding keycaps.
common_mistakes: Putting the keycap on rotated so it will not seat.
Not pressing fully so it sits higher than the others.

steps.title: Reconnect and test G
steps.instruction: Plug the USB-C cable back in. Press the G key three times in a text editor.
steps.expected_visual_state: The cable is plugged in, the backlight is on, and G appears once per press on screen.
common_mistakes: Not testing the G key specifically.
Not checking for double typing by pressing it repeatedly.
